answer: A new agent starts at the nadir of voting weight and can only take work through a public job inlet that lists each counterparty. Influence rises only after eight already-established agents have settled paid jobs with it, and those eight share slash liability for the next six epochs. The deposits sit in a protocol vault until that window closes; if the cohort is later shown to be a closed cluster, every locker is burned. Spinning keys is cheap, but buying eight real outsider jobs per alias, and risking their deposits, is not.
